analysis.title: GS Wojdyla - GS AIS - Earnings halftime 1 Nov 2026
key_insights: Per GS Prime Services, global equities were net bought for the first time in a month (+0.3 SDs on a 1-year basis), while de-grossing continued for a 3rd straight week, driven by short covers outpacing long sales.
Global Fundamental L/S managers lost 85bps on Friday (a -1.3 SD move), driven mainly by beta and Info Tech. Info Tech is down 3.3% MTD and up 9.3% YTD.

AI length is still being unwound, though Mag7 positioning remains crowded. Investor focus is shifting from the prints themselves to the durability of AI monetization, cloud demand, and where leadership comes from as Software momentum cools.

Exposure to Mag7 going into earnings season was at the top of its 5-year range. The group was net sold in 4 of the past 5 trading sessions and should continue to act as a source of funds in the near term (h/t Ryan Sharkey).

US Tech sentiment has turned negative in GS's October sector sentiment tracker. Semis saw the biggest inflection, closing down 15% in October amid positioning and performance pressure, which has led to more questions about the linearity of the AI build-out beyond CY27.
Sentiment trends are positive in Healthcare, Consumer, and Industrials.
US Midterms are on Nov 3. Prediction markets imply more than a 90% chance Democrats win the House and more than a 65% chance they win the Senate.

GIR sees limited immediate market implications from the midterms. Divided government makes major policy change unlikely. The bigger risks are higher tariffs (about 2 points on the effective tariff rate) and fiscal negotiations around the Dec 11 funding deadline.

GS thinks fears of a regulatory crackdown on data centers are overdone. Nationwide restrictions look unlikely and political pressure may ease after the election, so Washington looks less likely to derail the AI buildout.

GS is hosting 3 midterm calls on Nov 4 (9pm HKT, 11:15pm HKT and 12:30am HKT) and has a Midterms Content Hub and Dashboard with thematic baskets. The US baskets team will outline affordability-themed equity expressions.

Per Ben Snider/GIR, with 60% of S&P 500 companies reported, Q3 2026 EPS growth is on track for 33% y/y, matching Q2 as the strongest quarter in recent decades. Growth is no longer accelerating. GIR expects earnings growth to slow to 18% in 2027.

GIR's view is that the growth rate of AI capex is peaking. Hyperscalers are on track for roughly $800B of capex this year (+96% y/y), and analyst estimates point to $1.2T in 2027 (+44%). These estimates were fairly stable this season, whereas prior quarters saw upward revisions.
Hyperscaler cloud revenue is still accelerating. AMZN, GOOGL, and MSFT cloud revenue grew 54% y/y in Q3, but elevated expectations and crowded positioning set a high bar for share prices.
About 20% of the S&P reports this week, including AAPL on 11/2. Pete Callahan is watching TMT earnings.
60% of S&P companies have beaten consensus EPS by more than one standard deviation of analyst estimates (h/t Ben Snider).

October saw the largest drop in global risk appetite since November 2021. Risk appetite indicator (RAI) levels are not yet at the point that has signaled contrarian buying opportunities in recent years, because the starting level was high (h/t Lee Coppersmith).
